service.description: Fetch the branch of a remote kind repository from its remoteUrl into its bare mirror, created by the first fetch. The local branch is replaced by the remote one. Records lastFetchDate, lastFetchError and headCommitId on the repository. Refused in sim mode.

Fetch every remote kind repository whose fetchIntervalMinutes has passed since its lastFetchDate (for the fetch_AllGitRepositories_frequent ServiceJob). A repository that fails has its error recorded and logged, and the others are still fetched.

Push a repository's refs to its push mirror over SSH (pushMirrorRemoteId, pushMirrorRefs), each forced to the local one as it is when the push runs; nothing is deleted. Nothing for a repository with no push mirror. The framework's post-receive gitECA rule runs it async after each change; pushes of one repository take turns. Records lastPushMirrorDate and lastPushMirrorError in a transaction of their own, so a failure is kept. Refused in sim mode.
Make a repository ready: create the bare repository of a local kind (a local repository is also created on its first use), fetch a remote kind for the first time. A db kind needs nothing.

service.description: Keep the files matching patterns in Git LFS: a commit of the repository's .gitattributes with filter=lfs for each pattern it does not have. A git:// write of such a file stores its content as a content blob and commits its LFS pointer; git-lfs clients push and fetch it at /git/repositoryId.git/info/lfs.

parameter.name: patterns
parameter.description: gitattributes patterns (*.png, media/**); images, video, audio, PDFs and archives when empty

parameter.name: commitId
parameter.description: Empty when it had them all

service.description: Commit files of a local or db repository in one commit, with a message, as the current user (with the Moqui-User-Id trailer): what a page that edits a file saves with. Where it goes: the default branch, or branch (needs AT_GIT_REPOSITORY update); newBranch, made at branch's head (needs create); or with asProposal no branch at all: the commit becomes the head of the user's merge request into branch, opened or updated as by a push to refs/for/[branch] (view is enough; propose#MergeRequest), within the server's caps for a user with no push right (git-server review-max-push-bytes and review-max-account-bytes), and with no file kept in Git LFS. A branch moves as a push moves it: the branch rules are checked (a protected branch refuses with GitProtectedBranch), the pre events of gitECA rules of source write may refuse, the change is in the push log and the post events follow. Files: fileMap (path to its text or bytes), removePaths, renameMap (old path to new: a file or a directory, in the same commit as edits of it). expectedBlobIds is path to the blob the edit began from (from get#GitTree's objectId; empty text: no file there): when the path has another blob now nothing is committed, and the answer has no error but conflict true, errorCode GitFileChanged and conflictList, each path with expectedBlobId and currentBlobId, so a page shows both texts. authorName and authorEmail are the commit's author, given by the application with authorization disabled (an account's name and its confirmed address; a caller does not say who a commit is by), and the committer is then the server (git-server committer-name and committer-email). A proposal runs the pre events of gitECA rules as a push to refs/for/[branch] does (source push, transport internal). With authorization disabled and bypassBranchRules the branch rules are not checked. Refusals start with a code (docs/interfaces/Git-Hosting.md, Error codes): GitProtectedBranch, GitRefExists, GitArchived, GitNoSuchRef, GitStaleRef, GitReviewPushTooLarge, GitReviewQuota.

parameter.name: fileMap
parameter.description: Path to its new text (or bytes)

parameter.name: renameMap
parameter.description: Old path to new path

parameter.name: fileLocationMap
parameter.description: Path to a resource location whose bytes are its content (a staged upload): read as the server, so given with authorization disabled only

parameter.name: branch
parameter.description: The branch committed to, or the one a new branch or a proposal starts from and is for; the default branch when empty

parameter.name: newBranch
parameter.description: Make this branch at branch's head and commit to it

parameter.name: mergeRequestId
parameter.description: With asProposal: the user's open proposal to give the commit to; else the one of the same target and topic, else a new one

parameter.name: title
parameter.description: With asProposal: the merge request's title; the message's first line when empty

parameter.name: expectedBlobIds
parameter.description: Path to the blob id the edit began from

parameter.name: authorName
parameter.description: With authorization disabled only, as authorEmail

parameter.name: bypassBranchRules
parameter.description: Do not check the branch rules: an application's own write to a protected branch (release notes). With authorization disabled only; ignored otherwise

parameter.name: commitId
parameter.description: Empty when nothing changed, or on a conflict

parameter.name: refName
parameter.description: The ref that has the commit: the branch, or the merge request's head

parameter.name: errorCode
parameter.description: GitFileChanged with conflict

parameter.name: conflictList
parameter.description: Maps: path, expectedBlobId, currentBlobId

service.description: Make repositoryId a fork of sourceRepositoryId, a local or db repository the current user may view: a new repository of the same kind, in the source's fork network (forkNetworkId, the root's id, set on the source too when it had none; forkOfRepositoryId names the source), with the source's branches and tags as they are now as its own refs, its default branch, and its Git LFS objects. It shares the source's objects: a db fork has no object rows of its own (the network's are the root's rows, and what a fork adds is marked for its usage), a local fork reads the source's objects directory (objects/info/alternates) and keeps its new objects in its own directory (runtime/git/[repositoryId]). What a repository's readers read by id is decided by its refs, so a fork's commits are not read through its parent or the other way round. The service only checks view of the source: who may fork, into which id and repositoryPath, how many forks an account has and how wide the fork is seen are the application's rules, checked before it calls and set after (set#GitRepositoryPath, its own access records). Refused with GitRepositoryExists for an id in use. A repository with forks is not deleted (delete#GitRepository, GitHasForks).

parameter.name: localPath
parameter.description: For a local fork: its directory, as GitRepository.localPath (under the runtime directory unless absolute); runtime/git/[repositoryId] when empty. With authorization disabled only

service.description: The branches and tags that contain a commit (it is their head or an ancestor of it), for a commit's page. At most limit refs are asked, the default branch first, then the other branches and the tags by name, and at most git-server contains-max-commits (200,000) commits are read; truncated when there were more of either. Nothing out when the revision names no commit a reader reads.

parameter.name: limit
parameter.description: At most 500

parameter.name: refList
parameter.description: Maps: refName, refType, shortName, isDefaultBranch

service.description: Who brought commits to a repository: for each of commitIdList (full ids, at most 500) the user of the first push or write whose refs reached it (moqui.resource.GitCommitPush, read by its key; written with each change's events, at most git-server eca-max-commits commits a change). No entry for a commit that came by a mirror fetch or an import, or before pushers were kept, and none for a commit the caller does not read by id. For viewers.

parameter.name: pusherList
parameter.description: Maps: commitId, userId, username, updateId, pushDate

service.description: Delete the objects of db kind repositories that no ref reaches (and no change in progress or of the last git-server gc-reflog-days days needs) and that were not written or referenced in the last git-server gc-prune-days days; then repack: store the versions of each path as deltas of each other, the newest whole, compress rows written before the zlib format, and make delta chains deeper than git-server db-delta-depth shorter (for the gc_GitRepositories_daily ServiceJob). A repository whose refs reach a missing object is not collected. A local kind repository is repacked on disk instead: what is reachable (or needed as above) in one new pack, unreachable objects of the last gc-prune-days days kept loose, the packs and loose objects it replaced deleted; one with one pack and few loose objects is passed over. A repository that fails has its error recorded (lastGcResult) and logged, and the others still run.

parameter.name: repositoryId
parameter.description: Every db and local repository when empty

parameter.name: dryRun
parameter.description: Count what would be deleted and change nothing

parameter.name: timeoutMinutes
parameter.description: When repacking stops; the deletes are done first

parameter.name: results
parameter.description: A Map per repository: repositoryId, deletedCount, deletedBytes, repackedCount, savedBytes, objectCount, storedBytes, summary, or error

service.description: Decode every object of a db kind repository (applying its deltas) and check it against its id, and that every ref points to an object that is there. An error names the damaged objects.
Run the gitECA post events (ref-update, commit, tag, post-receive) of a pending GitUpdate, as the user who made it. Nothing when it is not pending (it ran, or another worker has it).

Run the post events of every pending GitUpdate, after putting back the ones a restart cut short (for the process_PendingGitUpdates_frequent ServiceJob). One that fails is recorded on its row and logged, and the others still run.

Delete GitUpdate rows in ecaStatus done or none whose updateDate is older than daysToKeep (for the clean_GitUpdates_daily ServiceJob). A row's GitUpdateRef rows go first. A row that cannot be removed is logged and the others still go.
What the current user may do in a repository: view (clone, read), create (new branches and tags), update (fast-forwards, merges, commit statuses) and delete (force, delete refs, settings, archive).

parameter.name: userId

For its viewers; a user without the update right is given no remoteAddress, no object id that no readable ref reaches now (the old value of a forced or deleted branch), and no row of a push to refs/for/ whose head is not read (a hidden merge request's).

Nothing out when the revision or the path names nothing; isFile when the path is a file (read it with get#GitBlob).

parameter.name: revision

service.description: For each line of the file at a path in a revision, the commit that last changed it, as runs of lines of one commit. Each commit passes the lines it did not change to the parent that has them; renames are not followed, so a file is blamed as far back as it has its path. Needs view. Nothing out when the revision names nothing or the path is not a file there. Refused: a binary file, a file kept in Git LFS, and past any of the git-server limits: a file over blame-max-bytes (1 MiB) or blame-max-lines (50,000), a history that needs more than blame-max-commits (10,000) commits read or blame-max-diffs (2,000) versions compared, and a blame that runs longer than blame-max-seconds (10). Within them it is still seconds of a service thread for a large file with a long history: a page that offers it to visitors rate limits its route.

parameter.name: revision
parameter.description: A branch, tag or commit; the default branch when empty

parameter.name: withLines
parameter.description: Each hunk with its lines, without their line endings

parameter.name: commitId
parameter.description: The commit the revision names

parameter.name: hunkList
parameter.description: In line order, Maps: startLine (from 1), lineCount, commitId, shortId, summary, authorName, authorEmail, authorDate, and with withLines lines (a List of text)

service.description: The tree at a revision, or a directory of it, as a zip or tar.gz file whose entries are under one directory named for the repository and the commit (mr-moqui-0123456789/). Files kept in Git LFS are archived with their content, a submodule as its empty directory. A link is a link entry, never followed here, when its target is relative and stays inside the archive; one with an absolute target or one that leaves the archive is left out and named in skippedList. Needs view. Nothing out when the revision names nothing or the path is not a directory there. archiveLocation is the absolute path of a file under runtime/tmp/git-archive on the node that answered: one file for each (repository, commit, path, format), which every caller asking for that archive is given, so serve it (ec.web.sendResourceResponse(archiveLocation, false, fileName)) and never delete, move or write it. It is removed six hours after its last use. Refused, before anything is written: a tree with an entry name an archive cannot hold safely (empty, '.', '..', '.git' in any case, with '/', a backslash or NUL, not UTF-8) or a name twice in one directory; a tree of more than git-server archive-max-bytes (256 MiB) of content, archive-max-files (50,000) entries (each tree read counts) or 64 directories deep; when archive-max-concurrent (2) archives are being made; when the files kept would pass archive-max-disk-bytes (2 GiB); and a format other than zip and tar.gz.

parameter.name: revision
parameter.description: A branch, tag or commit; the default branch when empty

parameter.name: format
parameter.description: zip or tar.gz (tgz)

parameter.name: path
parameter.description: A directory to archive; the whole tree when empty

parameter.name: archiveLocation
parameter.description: The file's absolute path

parameter.name: fileName
parameter.description: The name to offer: the top directory and the format's extension

parameter.name: contentBytes
parameter.description: The bytes of the files, before compression

parameter.name: skippedList
parameter.description: The paths of the links left out

parameter.name: refType

service.description: What head has that base lacks, as GitHub's compare: the merge base, the commits in head and not in base (oldest first, at most 250), ahead and behind, the files changed from the merge base to head with their line counts, and with withDiffs each file's diff (at most 300 files) as the moqui-diff html and as hunks of numbered lines for review. With checkMergeable a trial merge of head into base.

parameter.description: The target; the default branch when empty

parameter.name: head
parameter.description: The source

parameter.name: headRepositoryId
parameter.description: The repository head is a revision of: another one of the fork network of repositoryId, which the user may view too (a fork compared with its parent). Empty: repositoryId

parameter.name: includeHidden

service.description: Merge a source revision into a target branch as the current user, by method: GmmMerge (a merge commit), GmmFastForward (refused when the target has commits the source lacks), GmmSquash (one commit of the merged tree on the target) or GmmRebase (each commit of the source replayed on the target). Refused on a conflict (the paths in conflictPaths), when the target already has the source, and by the target's branch rules (a protected target changes through merge#MergeRequest). Needs update; the change runs the gitECA rules of source write. With checkOnly a trial merge that changes nothing (view is enough).

parameter.name: source
parameter.description: A branch, tag or commit

parameter.name: target
parameter.description: A branch

parameter.name: message
parameter.description: Of a merge commit or squash; a default when empty

parameter.name: includeHidden

parameter.name: commitId
parameter.description: The target's new head

service.description: Archive a repository: read only from now (pushes, ref writes, merges and writes refused), its open merge requests closed, left out of find#GitRepositories unless asked. Needs delete.
Make an archived repository writable again. Needs delete.
A repository's description, default branch (an existing branch) and default merge method (GmmMerge or GmmSquash). Needs delete. Its path is set#GitRepositoryPath's.

Delete a repository and everything the framework keeps of it: its refs and objects (the rows of a db kind, the directory of a local or remote kind), its Git LFS objects and locks, its push log (GitUpdate), commit statuses, webhooks, branch rules, merge requests and their reviewers, the redirects of paths it had, and its row. It cannot be undone. Needs delete, which is also the right to force a push and to change the repository's settings: an application that lets fewer users delete (an Owner, a typed confirmation) checks its own rule first and exposes its own service, not this one. Called with authorization off it deletes for any caller. It first marks the repository as going (archivedDate, committed at once), and every push and write reads the row again before it stores, so nothing is written to it from then; the rows go in this service's transaction; once that commits the directory is removed and the rows of the id are deleted once more, for what a push that was already storing left. A rollback keeps everything and sets the mark back. The directory is removed only when, read from the disk with its links followed, it is under the runtime directory (and is not it), looks like a bare repository (HEAD and objects/), and no other repository's row names it, a directory in it or one it is in; else it is left and named in directoryKept. Left too: the content blobs of its large and LFS objects, which gc#ContentBlobs collects when no other repository has them, and webhook deliveries already queued. Refused: a repository that holds a drive (delete the drive), and one a row of another component still refers to through a foreign key (the application removes its own rows first: Mantle's project links, a Smithy repository). A repository others were forked from is refused too (GitHasForks: its forks read its objects; delete them first, or archive it); a fork is deleted alone, its objects staying the network's until a collection lets go of those no ref reaches. Whether a repository with open merge requests or release assets may go is the application's rule.

parameter.name: directoryKept
parameter.description: Its directory, left where it is

service.description: What repositories store now, for an application's own quota code (it need not read GitObject or GitLfsObject): one repositoryId, a repositoryIdList (at most 1000), or both. Not for a visitor's route: a db repository costs a grouped read of its object rows and a local or remote one a walk of its directory, each time. Read from the rows and the directory as they are, so it is current right after a push; GitRepository.storedBytes and objectCount are only gc#GitRepositories' record of its last run. Needs view: a repository the user may not view, or that is not there, is left out of usageList. Called with authorization off (a gitECA rule's actions, the LFS upload check) it answers every repository asked that is there.

parameter.name: repositoryIdList
parameter.description: Ids, or a comma separated text

parameter.name: usageList
parameter.description: In the order asked, Maps: repositoryId, repositoryKind (db, local, remote), storedBytes (db: the object rows as stored, compressed and as deltas, with the content blobs of large objects, each counted in full though the same content is stored once; local and remote: the files of the directory), objectCount (db only), lfsBytes and lfsObjectCount (the Git LFS objects uploaded to it)

service.description: The service git-server lfs-upload-check-service names: asked before Git LFS objects new to a repository are accepted, by the batch API (once for a batch, with every object it would add), by an upload itself (one object), and by a write of an LFS-tracked file through Moqui (a git:// location, commit#GitFiles). It runs as the user, with authorization off. An error it adds refuses the upload, and its text is what the git-lfs client shows; a service that fails refuses too. It is asked a second time once an object is the repository's, with stored true and uploadBytes 0: uploads that were each within a limit when they asked can pass it together, and the one refused then is taken back. So a service that adds uploadBytes to what get#GitRepositoryUsage counts needs no change to be exact at the end of concurrent uploads. Until then each upload in flight may hold up to lfs-max-object-size of content not yet counted, and a refused upload's content stays until gc#ContentBlobs.

parameter.name: uploadBytes
parameter.description: The bytes of the objects that would be added; 0 when stored

parameter.name: stored
parameter.description: The second ask: the objects are the repository's already, and counted in its usage

parameter.name: objectList
parameter.description: Maps: oid, size

service.description: Set the path git URLs carry for a repository (moqui/mr-moqui: /git/moqui/mr-moqui.git, SSH moqui/mr-moqui.git, and the page URL on a public-site host), or clear it with an empty repositoryPath (the repository is then addressed by its id, which always works). Needs update: an application that lets fewer users rename or move a repository checks its own rule first. A path is one to eight segments of letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', none starting with '.' or '-' or ending in .git or .lock. Paths that differ only in case are one path (repositoryPathKey, the path in lower case, is what is unique and looked up); the path is kept as written. Refused: a path of one segment other than the repository's own id (a one-segment address is an id's), and another repository's path. The path the repository had is kept as a GitRepositoryPathRedirect, so clones of the old address keep working, and a redirect from the new path (a repository that once had it) is removed. This service is the only writer of repositoryPath.
The branch rules of a repository that name a ref (every rule without one), and what they ask together. For its viewers.

parameter.name: allowedMergeMethods
parameter.description: Empty: any

service.description: Create or update a branch rule. Needs delete on the repository.
Delete a branch rule. Needs delete on its repository.
A check of a commit by outside CI, in GitHub's status shape. Needs a push right on the repository (a CI user with an access token); the commit must be in the repository.

parameter.name: context
parameter.description: default when empty

parameter.name: target_url

parameter.description: A commit, or a branch or tag

parameter.name: commitIdList
parameter.description: Full commit ids, for a log page

service.description: The webhooks of a repository, the secret left out. Needs delete on the repository.

Create or update a webhook: an http or https URL, the events (push, tag, merge_request; all when empty), the secret its deliveries are signed with (kept when left empty on an update), active. Needs delete on the repository.
Delete a webhook; its deliveries not yet sent are cancelled. Needs delete on its repository.
Send a ping event to a webhook now, recorded as a delivery. Needs delete on its repository.
The deliveries of a webhook, newest first, each with its attempts' errors: the delivery log. Needs delete on its repository.

parameter.name: deliveryList

service.description: The send service of SystemMessage type GitWebhook: POST the message's JSON to its webhook's URL with X-Moqui-Event, X-Moqui-Delivery and, with a secret, X-Hub-Signature-256 (sha256= the HMAC-SHA256 of the body). Internal addresses are refused unless git-server webhook-private-network. A status that is not 2xx is an error, so the delivery is retried.
For the framework's post-receive gitECA rule (Git.gitecas.xml): a push event per branch that changed and a tag event per tag, to each active webhook of the repository that takes it.

parameter.name: refUpdates
parameter.description: As org.moqui.GitServices.process#GitEca's

service.description: Any other event of a repository (merge_request, with an action) to each active webhook that takes it: payload as the body, with event, action, repository and sender.

Send again the webhook deliveries that failed, each after a wait that doubles with its failures (1, 2, 4 ... minutes); after retryLimit failures it is in error and no longer tried (for the retry_GitWebhookDeliveries_frequent ServiceJob). One that fails is logged and the others are still tried.
